title: BM25 ranking function
text: BM25 is a bag-of-words ranking function that scores documents by term frequency, inverse document frequency and document length normalization. Parameters k1 and b control term saturation and length normalization. It remains a strong baseline for lexical retrieval.

title: Dense retrieval with bi-encoders
text: Dense retrieval encodes queries and documents into vectors with a bi-encoder and ranks by cosine similarity. It handles paraphrase and vocabulary mismatch well but can miss exact identifiers, rare entities and numbers.

title: Reciprocal rank fusion
text: Reciprocal rank fusion combines ranked lists from different retrievers by summing 1 over a constant plus rank. It needs no score calibration, which makes it popular for hybrid search that merges BM25 and embedding results.

title: Cross-encoder reranking
text: A cross-encoder reads the query and a candidate document together and outputs a relevance score. It is far more accurate than a bi-encoder but too slow for the whole corpus, so it reranks only the top candidates from a first-stage retriever, adding latency.

title: Query rewriting and decomposition
text: Query rewriting reformulates a user question to improve recall. Decomposition splits a multi-part question into sub-queries that are searched separately, which helps comparison and multi-hop questions where no single document contains the full answer.

title: Agentic retrieval loops
text: In agentic retrieval a language model decides which tool calls to make, inspects results, rewrites failing queries and chooses when to stop. Risks include runaway loops, redundant searches, higher latency and cost, so a step budget and stopping criteria are needed.

title: Normalized discounted cumulative gain
text: nDCG measures ranking quality with graded relevance, discounting gains logarithmically by position and normalizing by the ideal ranking. nDCG at 10 is the standard headline metric in benchmarks such as BEIR.

title: Recall at k and MRR
text: Recall at k is the fraction of relevant documents found in the top k results. Mean reciprocal rank rewards placing the first relevant result high. Recall of the first stage caps what a reranker can achieve.

title: BEIR benchmark
text: BEIR is a heterogeneous benchmark of 18 retrieval datasets for zero-shot evaluation. It showed that BM25 is a robust baseline and that dense models trained on one domain often generalize poorly to others.

title: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
text: An LLM judge grades answers against a rubric or reference. Judges show position bias, verbosity bias and self-preference, so they should be calibrated against human labels on a sample before the scores are trusted.

title: Approximate nearest neighbor indexes
text: HNSW and IVF indexes trade a small loss in recall for large speedups in vector search. Tuning efSearch or nprobe moves along the recall versus latency curve. Quantization reduces memory at a further cost in accuracy.

title: Inverted index internals
text: An inverted index maps each term to a postings list of document ids and frequencies. Compression, skip lists and block-max pruning make lexical search fast on very large collections, and sharding spreads the index across machines.

title: Chunking strategies for retrieval
text: Documents are split into chunks before embedding. Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding, and chunks that are too small lose context. Overlapping windows and structure-aware splitting at headings usually improve retrieval.

title: Online relevance measurement
text: Production search teams measure impact with A/B tests on click-through rate, reformulation rate and abandonment. Interleaving gives higher sensitivity with less traffic. Offline metrics only help if they correlate with these online outcomes.

title: Caching in search systems
text: Result caches and embedding caches cut latency and load for repeated queries. Head queries have high hit rates while long-tail queries do not. Invalidation must balance freshness against consistency when documents change.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation failure modes
text: RAG fails when retrieval misses the evidence, when irrelevant context distracts the generator, or when the model ignores the context. Diagnosing requires evaluating retrieval and generation separately before looking at end-to-end answer quality.

title: Neural network activation functions
text: ReLU, GELU and tanh activations affect gradient flow and training convergence speed. Saturating activations suffer vanishing gradients in deep networks, which slows convergence.

title: React code splitting
text: Code splitting with dynamic imports and React.lazy defers loading of components until needed, reducing initial bundle size and page load time.
